content.text:
A client uses **three HTTP methods** on the MCP endpoint in the 2025-11-25 spec:

| Method | When the client uses it | Requirement level |
|---|---|---|
| **POST** | Every JSON-RPC message the client sends (requests, notifications, responses) is a new POST. The `Accept` header must list both `application/json` and `text/event-stream`. | **MUST** |
| **GET** | To open an SSE stream so the server can send messages without the client posting first (`Accept: text/event-stream`). Also used to resume a dropped stream, with a `Last-Event-ID` header. The server may answer 405 if it doesn't offer a stream. | **MAY** (resuming is **SHOULD**) |
| **DELETE** | To end a session it no longer needs, sending the `MCP-Session-Id` header. The server may refuse with 405. | **SHOULD** |

The spec also says the server "MUST provide a single HTTP endpoint path… that supports both POST and GET methods." So POST and GET are the core of the transport, and DELETE is only for ending a session.

**Source**
- Final URL: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/transports (HTTP 200, no redirects)
- Fetch time (`evidenceRecord.fetchedAt`): **2026-10-09T17:39:14.758Z**. The page was fetched live, not from cache.

**How I found the page:** the map search for "streamable http" returned only two pages, the `2026-07-28` and `draft` versions at `.../basic/transports/streamable-http`. The 2025-11-25 spec has no separate Streamable HTTP page; it's a section of the Transports page. I found that page with a second map search ("2025-11-25 transports") and confirmed the section is on it before scraping.
